mcp.meta.description: Connect your own AI client to a read-only MCP server and ask it about my case studies, decisions, career and posts, with the source of every answer.
mcp.title: My portfolio's MCP
mcp.lead: A remote, read-only MCP server. You connect it from the AI client you already use and ask it about my case studies, my decisions, my career, my skills and my posts. Every answer comes with its source and a link.
mcp.what: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard an agent uses to call other people's tools. This server speaks Streamable HTTP with no session: every message is a POST with JSON-RPC and the answer is JSON. It asks for no token because everything it returns is already public on the site.
mcp.facts.versions: Protocol versions it accepts: {versions}. I checked them on modelcontextprotocol.io on November 26, 2026.
mcp.facts.limits: Limits: {visitor} calls every 10 minutes per IP, {match} job description matches per hour and {daily} calls a day for everyone.
mcp.connect.title: Connect it in two minutes
mcp.connect.pending: Not tested yet on the preview
mcp.connect.ask: Then ask it, for example: "Which architecture decisions did Camilo make in Synergos?".
mcp.catalog.title: What the server publishes
mcp.catalog.lead: This list is not written by hand: it comes from the server's own tools/list when the page is built.
mcp.tester.title: Protocol tester
mcp.tester.lead: Send the messages yourself and see every request and every response exactly as they travel, with the milliseconds.
mcp.tester.empty: You have not sent anything yet. Start with the first step.
mcp.tester.failed: The server did not answer ({reason}). This is not an empty list: the call failed.
mcp.tester.badJson: The arguments are not a valid JSON object.
mcp.tester.noscript: The tester needs JavaScript. The URL, the steps and the catalog on this page work without it.
mcp.tester.fictional: The sample job description is fictional.
mcp.limits.title: What it does not do
mcp.limits.body: It writes nothing, calls no model and reads no visitor messages, accounts or comments. It does not store your arguments: each call only adds 1 to the daily counter.
